cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I changed the meeting time. Did you change the room? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Yes. That's my half of why nobody met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why didn't you tell me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I should have. Now tell me where your half of the meeting went.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I changed the meeting time. Did you change the room?

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. That's my half of why nobody met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why didn't you tell me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I should have. Now tell me where your half of the meeting went.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I hid the first complaint letter. What happened to the second?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've admitted hiding a letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I'm not asking you to stand in the spotlight alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a third one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's put our envelopes down in order.

cards.title: It Was Foreshadowed
cards.instruction: Turn the failure into a planned turning point by returning to earlier details that now appear to predict it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The collapsed cake was foreshadowed by that first wobble. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ignored the wobble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I allowed the audience to discover its significance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There is no cake now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. The empty stand pays off the warning beautifully.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There is no cake now.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tent falling is our planned turning point. Remember the loose peg I mentioned?

beats.text: And the earlier remark about waterproof coats has become remarkably well placed.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. When I said the evening would flow, I meant this kitchen flood. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You meant conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Water is now the dominant topic. A remarkably accurate forecast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't predict a burst pipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I said we'd need to open up. The plumbing listened first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I said the evening would flow, I meant this kitchen flood.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You meant conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Water is now the dominant topic. A remarkably accurate forecast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't predict a burst pipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I said we'd need to open up. The plumbing listened first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My forecast said sunny. Clearly I meant your reaction to the refund.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The holiday was ruined by rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which created the refund and your brightened outlook.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A symbol of optimism. You must read the whole prediction generously.

cards.title: Reverse the Score
cards.instruction: Turn each apparent loss into a new category of victory, then invite comparison on those changing terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Last in the race, first in appreciating the route. Beat that. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a speed contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. A narrow category. How many wildflowers did you notice?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I noticed the finish line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I also win for variety of attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last in the race, first in appreciating the route. Beat that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a speed contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A narrow category. How many wildflowers did you notice?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I noticed the finish line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I also win for variety of attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The small trophy is better. It shows restraint.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the consolation prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. How gracefully can your enormous cup fit in a cupboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine says first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And mine doesn't need to shout. Another victory in modesty.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. We wanted somewhere to belong. This leaking cottage can still be ours. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It may cost our savings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We hoped for a home, not an untouched savings account beside someone else's house.
